title: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook (January 2027) — the horizon-roll edition: the first STEO carrying 2028 forecast lines, and the first published on the far side of the 2026-12-11 funding cliff
source: EST: eia.gov/outlooks/steo/release_schedule.php, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial research (HTTP 200, 54,906 bytes — byte-identical to the eia-steo-2026-12-08 lane's 2026-09-08 pull, so the page has not moved). Read from the RAW HTML table rather than a converted rendering: the January 2027 row is "January 2027 | 01/12/2027" with a blank Notes cell, and the release window is stated on the same page as 12:00-12:15 pm ET. Reproduces independently from the same page's stated rule ("the release of the STEO on the first Tuesday following the first Thursday of each month", with the footnote "If a Federal holiday falls on the Monday before the normal release date the release is delayed until Wednesday"): 2027-01-07 is a Thursday, the following Tuesday is 01-12, and 2027-01-11 is a Monday that is not a Federal holiday (New Year's Day 2027 falls Friday 01-01 and MLK Day falls Monday 01-18), so no adjustment applies. Filed estimate on the two counts every EIA entry on this calendar records, neither of them date doubt: this calendar defines no `confirmed` prefix for the EIA (the standing schema gap eia-steo-2026-09-09 named), and this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep
notes: Canonical entry written by this event's own never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09), promoting the sole prior proposal eia-steo-2027-01-12.from-eia-steo-2026-12-08.json. That proposal handed this lane two claims and explicitly flagged the second as unverified; BOTH are now settled from primaries, and they settle in opposite directions. (1) THE HORIZON ROLL IS REAL AND IS NOW VERIFIED — the proposing lane could not check it and said so. EIA's own archived editions carry the proof in their U.S. energy market indicators table: archives/nov25.pdf reads columns 2024 | 2025 | 2026, and archives/jan26.pdf (cover date January 13, 2026, matching the schedule table) reads 2025 | 2026 | 2027. The January edition drops the oldest year and adds an out-year, so the 2027-01-12 edition is the first STEO to publish 2028 lines — including the first EIA 2028 national electricity-consumption forecast, which is the out-year the ai-energy-constraint.md demand leg has never had. That, not the funding cliff, is this edition's largest information increment. (2) THE PUBLICATION RISK IS REAL BUT THE PROPOSAL'S ANALOGUE IS VOID. Exposure is confirmed: FY2027 Energy-Water never reached the House floor (approved by full committee 2026-05-20, 34-25; only MilCon-VA, Agriculture and National Security-State have passed the full House; the Senate has reported none), so DOE/EIA is squarely inside PL 119-103 and inside any lapse beginning 00:00 2026-12-12 — which would make 2027-01-12 day 32. But cr-expiry-2026-12-11's 35-day 2018-19 lame-duck analogue CANNOT be carried across to publication risk: Energy-Water was one of the five FY2019 bills enacted in the September 2018 minibus, so DOE was fully funded and the 2018-19 shutdown never touched EIA at all. The analogue that does apply is the 43-day 2025 lapse (2025-10-01 -> 2025-11-12), and it is duration-matched and favorable: BOTH scheduled editions published, archives/oct25.pdf cover-dated October 7, 2025 (day 7) and archives/nov25.pdf cover-dated November 12, 2025 (day 43, the lapse's final day). Filed `low` on the sibling entries' reasoning, and the corridor reinforces it rather than raising it. Unlike eia-steo-2026-12-08, which published into an FOMC day-1 SEP freeze with 21 tracked ids inside +/-5 days, this edition has THREE (ism-services-2027-01-07, opex-2027-01-15, fomc-blackout-start-2027-01-16), none of them on the day, and it publishes four days BEFORE the blackout for the January 26-27 FOMC opens (FED: fomccalendars.htm, fetched direct 2026-09-09 — January 26-27 carries no SEP asterisk). That makes 2027-01-12 the cleanest attribution environment for a STEO this calendar has, and therefore the first honest out-of-sample test of the STEO-day null rather than another un-attributable day.
